Year over year total mixes a partial month
The % +/- Total and Total Company +/- include the partial current month against a full month last year.
Overstates any decline by several points until the month closes.
Compute through the last closed month.
Enhancer burn rate divides one week by three
Used Since Last Order is the latest week only, divided by 3 weeks since the order. The Usage tab holds the real weekly counts.
Days of Stock Left is wrong by about 3x for fast movers.
Average the Usage tab cycles, as this dashboard does.
Two different order recommendations
The Totals tab and the Order tab each hold an order quantity, and they do not use the same cover rule.
The order you place depends on which tab you read.
Pick one cover target in weeks and derive the order from it.
PAR sheets have no PAR
Counts only, with free text units. Ashland blank, Massillon last edited Oct 29.
No shortage flags, no auto order, no way to tell stale from fresh.
Structured count form (item, unit, count, par) per store per order day.
Sales vs Orders tab starts Oct 6
Net sales read $0.00 before Oct 12, so the order ratio covers only a few weeks.
This dashboard recomputes it from the monthly daily sales.
Point the tab at the daily sales grid.
Tip pay period labels drift
From April to July the sheet labels periods starting Saturday, while the rest start Sunday. Wadsworth 6/22 to 7/5 in 2025 shows $3,808 against about $1,850 normal.
Year over year tip comparisons are only clean for the last eight periods, which is what this dashboard uses.
Standardize labels to the Sunday start and check the 2025 Wadsworth period.
Closed days are blank, not zero
Jan 25 (all three stores) and Apr 5 (Easter) have no sales logged.
Treated as closed in this dashboard. Averages exclude them.
Keep blank for closures.
Labor percent is a simple average
The sheet's Monthly Average is the mean of daily percentages. Dollar weighted figures here differ by up to about 0.6 points.
Small, but a low sales day with high labor pulls the sheet average up.
Report labor dollars and labor % weighted by sales.
